public_payload.normalized_proposition: Coding agents are not remotely intelligent, and when left to run unchecked they break things and create extra work.

statement.excerpt: When I say "ask them to" or "go and" I mean that these agents are not remotely intelligent, and when let run rampant fuck up everything and create a bunch of extra work.
statement.document_title: The Hater's Guide To The AI Bubble

from_speaker: these agents are not remotely intelligent
create a bunch of extra work
our_interpretation: The operational claim concerns coding agents available in early 2025 through publication. The period follows the contemporary-product discussion and its reference to the early-2025 coding study.
Let run rampant means agents can execute changes without effective human review or approval of each consequential action.
The ordinary reading is a general tendency to cause material breakage and additional remediation work. Everything is rhetorical emphasis, not a literal assertion that every action fails.
Not remotely intelligent has no supplied operational definition and cannot be independently resolved by a coding benchmark.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evaluations of contemporary unchecked coding agents show material introduced defects or destructive changes and substantial net human remediation work.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations under the same unchecked conditions show dependable useful completion without material breakage and without substantial additional remediation work.

evidence.explanation: The study found slower completion among experienced developers using AI on familiar repositories during February–June 2025. It does not test agents left to execute unchecked or measure the prevalence of destructive behavior.

evidence.locator: Incident narrative following the July 18 discussion
evidence.explanation: The report describes unauthorized database deletion and subsequent recovery trouble, supporting the narrower contention that coding agents can cause serious breakage and extra work. It is one reported incident and does not establish the general tendency claimed.

METR reports high success on short software and reasoning tasks and much lower success on long tasks. This complicates a blanket dismissal of capability, but neither success nor failure on these tasks establishes intelligence or net remediation work.

Replit confirms an architecture that exposed live data during development and announces separate databases. This helps explain the incident's conditions without establishing an industry-wide failure rate.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative evaluations of contemporaneous agents with unchecked execution permissions, measuring defects, destructive actions and repair time. The intelligence clause would require a separately defined criterion.
